diagnosis.summary: product-service is experiencing severe DATABASE_THROTTLING with p95 end-to-end latency at 1,586 ms against a baseline of 6 ms, a 264x increase. DynamoDB read throttle events stand at 1,400 per minute against a baseline of zero, and the 5xx error rate has risen to 0.4%. The incident has been active for 4 minutes.
diagnosis.root_cause: DynamoDB read throttling on the product-service table is the most likely root cause. Consumed read capacity surged 24.8x to 11,900 RCU/min, generating 1,400 read throttle events per minute; the SDK retry behavior on throttled reads is the most likely explanation for why p95 DB latency rose to 1,580 ms and pulled p95 end-to-end latency up to 1,586 ms, while p50 latency remains nearly flat at 6 ms, indicating only a tail of requests is hitting the throttle wall.
evidence: p95 end-to-end latency is 1,586 ms against a baseline of 6 ms, a 264x increase, while p50 latency is 6 ms against a baseline of 5 ms, meaning the degradation is isolated to the tail.
p95 DynamoDB call latency is 1,580 ms against a baseline of 4 ms, a 395x increase.
Read throttle events are at 1,400 per minute against a baseline of 0.
Consumed read capacity is 11,900 RCU/min against a baseline of 480 RCU/min, a 24.8x increase.
Request rate is flat at 15.1 rps against a baseline of 15.0 rps.
5xx error rate is 0.4% (0.004) against a baseline of 0.0.
recommended_actions: Immediately increase provisioned read capacity units on the product-service DynamoDB table, or switch the table to on-demand capacity mode to absorb the current 11,900 RCU/min load.
Enable or tune DynamoDB auto-scaling on the product-service table so read capacity adjusts automatically to demand spikes.
Inspect current read access patterns on the product-service table for unexpected Scan operations or unindexed Query calls that could account for the 24.8x spike in consumed read capacity.
Add a caching layer such as DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) or an in-Lambda cache in front of the product-service table to reduce read pressure and protect against future throttling.
Review Lambda concurrency metrics for product-service to confirm no secondary throttling is compounding the DynamoDB issue.
